column2: Analyse School Performance — DfE tool replacing RAISEonline. Shows school performance against national benchmarks using KS2/KS4 data. Lagging indicator — tells you where you are, not why or what next.

Inspection Data Summary Report — Ofsted's pre-inspection data pack. Auto-generated for each school before an inspection. Shows key metrics inspectors will focus on. You should know what's in yours before they arrive.
Multi-Year School Analysis — DfE longitudinal tool. Shows performance trends over multiple years rather than single-year snapshots. Useful for spotting trajectory, not just position.

DfE public tool (formerly School Performance Tables). Lets you compare schools using published KS2/KS4 data, absence, finance. Available at compare-school-performance.service.gov.uk. Your 13 schools' data is public here.

National Pupil Database — DfE's central relational database of all pupils in England. Fed by School Census, exam results, attendance, exclusions. Extracts delivered as CSV flat files. Not XML. The national stats warehouse.

Common Transfer File — XML format used for peer-to-peer pupil transfer between schools. When a pupil moves, sending school exports CTF, receiving school imports it into their MIS. Does NOT feed the NPD.

Termly statutory return submitted by every school via their MIS (Arbor, SIMS etc.) to DfE. Covers pupil demographics, attendance, exclusions, SEN provision, free school meals. Feeds the NPD. Three per year: autumn, spring, summer.

Fischer Family Trust Aspire — predictive analytics tool. Generates pupil-level estimates/targets based on prior attainment and national patterns. Widely used for target-setting and identifying underperformance. Subscription service.

Free benchmarking tool from FFT. Lighter version of FFT Aspire. Lets schools compare performance against similar schools using contextual filters. Good for quick benchmarking without full FFT subscription.

Schools Business Intelligence — DfE's internal analytics platform for regional directors and advisors. Not typically available to schools/Trusts directly. Used by DfE to monitor school performance at scale.

Real-time pulse survey tool for staff wellbeing and school climate. Captures "tone" data — how staff feel, engagement levels, workload perception. Quick, regular micro-surveys rather than annual staff surveys.
Multi Academy Trust — a group of academies operating under a single trust with shared governance, central functions, and accountability. DRB Ignite is a MAT with 13 primary schools.

Secondary school accountability measure. Compares pupils' KS4 results against pupils nationally with similar KS2 starting points. Score of 0 = average progress; positive = above average. Applies to secondary, not DRB's primaries.

Secondary school accountability measure. Average grade across 8 GCSE subjects (English, maths, 3 EBacc, 3 open). Raw attainment, not progress. Again secondary — DRB is primary, so KS2 measures apply instead.

Key Stage 2 — end of primary school (Year 6, age 10-11). National tests (SATs) in reading, maths, GPS (grammar/punctuation/spelling). Writing is teacher-assessed. This is DRB Ignite's main accountability measure.
Key Stage 4 — end of secondary school (Year 11, age 15-16). GCSEs. Measured by Progress 8 and Attainment 8. Not directly relevant to DRB's primary schools but useful context.

Self-Evaluation Form — school's own assessment of its strengths and areas for development, structured around the Ofsted framework. Narrative-heavy, often evidence-light. Your slides reference making these more data-driven.
School Improvement Plan (also SDP — School Development Plan). Outlines priorities, actions, success criteria, and timelines for school improvement. Should be evidence-based but often isn't.

Condition Improvement Fund — DfE capital funding for academies and sixth-form colleges. Competitive bid process for building repairs/improvements. Your estates slides propose using data to strengthen CIF bids.

School Condition Allocation — formulaic capital funding given directly to large MATs (those with 5+ academies and at least 3,000 pupils). DRB Ignite likely receives SCA rather than bidding for CIF. Used for prioritised maintenance.

General Annual Grant — the main revenue funding academies receive from ESFA. Based on pupil numbers and the national funding formula. Replaces the delegated budget that maintained schools get from their LA.

Education and Skills Funding Agency — the DfE body that funds and regulates academies and further education. Monitors MAT finances. Issues Financial Notices to Improve if concerned. Your finance slides should acknowledge their oversight role.

Pupil Premium — additional government funding for disadvantaged pupils (those eligible for FSM in last 6 years, looked-after children, service children). Schools must demonstrate impact. A key accountability metric.

Free School Meals — eligibility indicator used as a proxy for disadvantage. "Ever 6 FSM" (eligible at any point in last 6 years) determines Pupil Premium funding. Often the primary deprivation measure in school data.

Special Educational Needs and Disabilities — pupils with learning difficulties or disabilities requiring additional support. Ranges from SEN Support (school-based) to EHCP (legally binding plan with named provision).

Education, Health and Care Plan — legal document for children/young people with significant SEND. Specifies provision the LA must fund. Replaced Statements of SEN in 2014. Schools must deliver what's in the plan.

English as an Additional Language — pupils whose first language is not English. A cohort definition for tracking and reporting. Ranges from newly arrived (significant support needed) to fully fluent (minimal impact).

Cloud-based MIS (Management Information System) used by DRB Ignite schools. Handles pupil records, attendance, assessment, behaviour, Census returns, timetabling. Your primary data source for integration.

Child Protection Online Monitoring System — safeguarding and welfare software. Logs concerns, incidents, actions. Used by DSLs and pastoral staff. Contains sensitive data — important for GDPR considerations. Integration point, not replacement.

Management Information System — the core school database (Arbor, SIMS, Bromcom etc.). Holds pupil records, attendance, assessment, timetable, Census data. The single source of truth for pupil-level data.
School Information Management System — legacy MIS by Capita (now ESS). Still used in many schools. Being replaced by cloud-based alternatives like Arbor and Bromcom. DRB uses Arbor, not SIMS.

Microsoft's business intelligence and data visualisation tool. You'll use this as the DISPLAY layer — dashboards, reports, interactive visuals. It shows what's in the data; the innovation is in how data is structured before it reaches Power BI.
Designated Safeguarding Lead — the person in each school responsible for child protection. Logs concerns in CPOMS. Must be trained to Level 3. Every school must have one; often the head or a deputy.

Office for Standards in Education — inspects and regulates schools. Current framework (2019) judges: Quality of Education, Behaviour & Attitudes, Personal Development, Leadership & Management. Grades: Outstanding, Good, RI, Inadequate.

Requires Improvement — Ofsted grade 3 (of 4). School is not yet Good. Triggers increased monitoring and support. A school rated RI will be reinspected within 30 months. Significant pressure on leadership.
Department for Education — the government department responsible for education and children's services in England. Publishes ASP, IDSR, runs NPD, sets policy, funds via ESFA.

General Data Protection Regulation — data protection law. Key principles: lawful basis, data minimisation, purpose limitation, storage limitation, accuracy, accountability. Your federated architecture addresses this by keeping PII local.

Personally Identifiable Information — any data that can identify an individual (name, UPN, DOB, address). In your federated model, PII never leaves the school. Only anonymised patterns are shared centrally.

Unique Pupil Number — 13-character identifier assigned to every pupil in England. Stays with them across schools. Used in Census, CTF transfers, and NPD. The key linking field across government datasets.

Information Commissioner's Office — the UK's data protection regulator. Enforces GDPR/Data Protection Act 2018. Can fine organisations for breaches. Your privacy-by-architecture approach is designed to exceed their requirements.

Red Amber Green — traffic-light rating system used ubiquitously in education for quick visual assessment. Red = concern, Amber = monitor, Green = on track. Simple but limited — your structured approach goes deeper.

Continuing Professional Development — ongoing training for teachers and staff. Your slides propose structuring CPD as a skills graph (prerequisites → capabilities) rather than a flat list of courses attended.

Return on Investment — ratio of benefit to cost. Your finance slides propose measuring interventions by ROI: "Intervention X returns £4 per £1 spent." Moves from "how much did we spend?" to "what did the spending achieve?"
Value for Money — a governance requirement for public-funded bodies. Trusts must demonstrate VFM in spending decisions. Currently often claimed in narrative; your approach proves it with data.

English Baccalaureate — secondary performance measure covering English, maths, sciences, a language, and history or geography at GCSE. Not directly relevant to DRB's primaries but context for KS4 discussions.

Looked After Children (also CLA — Children Looked After) — children in the care of the local authority. Attract Pupil Premium Plus funding (higher rate). A priority cohort for tracking and intervention.
Get Data about Schools — DfE's public data download service. Replaced the old performance tables download. Lets you pull school-level data including finance, workforce, performance for analysis.
RAISEonline — the predecessor to ASP. Retired in 2017. If anyone mentions RAISE, they mean ASP. Some older staff may still use the term out of habit.

AI architecture where each school runs its own model locally, shares only anonymised patterns centrally, and receives improved models back. No PII moves. Same approach Google uses for phone keyboard prediction.

The CAUSE — the factor that drives an outcome. Attendance, engagement, prerequisite skills, teaching method. Your core argument: we should measure and manage independent variables, not just count dependent ones.
The OUTCOME — the result we measure (test scores, grades, Progress 8). Lagging indicator. Most school data only captures this. Your approach captures the independent variables that cause it.

Directed graph of 459 skills, each with 5 observable criteria, parent skills (prerequisites), and offspring skills (what it enables). Diagnoses root causes rather than symptoms. "Emma hasn't failed maths — she hasn't consolidated working memory."
